newsitem.title: JAPAN: Early Asia crude sentiment firms on Indonesia fire.
newsitem.headline: Early Asia crude sentiment firms on Indonesia fire.

text.p: Crude prices were steady in early Asia on Tuesday with a fire at an Indonesian oil rig lending some bullish sentiment to regional markets, traders said.

Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Tuesday that a fire on an offshore rig near the town of Balikpapan in East Kalimantan Province had resulted in a precautionary shutdown of both the Attaka and Santan oil fields.
Brokers pegged notional values of cash Brent at $18.85/18.90 a barrel for October, a 2 to 3 cent gain over Monday levels.
Activity in both Indonesian and Abu Dhabi grades was expected in afternoon trade, traders said.
"We should see some buyers moving now following the Indonesia allocation," said a trader with a Japanese refiner.
In its September allocations, released on Monday, Indonesia increased heavy Minas export volumes slightly, but sharply cut heavy Widuri and Cinta exports.
"Cinta and Widuri look a little bit tighter this month, and could support other heavy grades," the trader added.
Traders said talk for Oman and Abu Dhabi grades had already begun with a flurry of trading likely on Tuesday afternoon.
"Our group is looking at Murban, Lower Zakum, Umm Shaim," said one trader.
Looking further out into October markets, traders said values were likely to firm.
"We're expecting Abu Dhabi grades to move up to ADNOC plus 20 or 25 (cents)," said a Japan trader.
"In terms of Oman, it depends to a large degree on demand from China and Taiwan, but the level could be around MPM plus 12 to 15 (cents)," he added.
Traders said uncertainty about Iraqi barrels headed east and the prospect of protracted Yemeni term contract negotiations would continue to support prices. -- P.Lardner/Tokyo
